descriptionChirho: The feminine noun shav'ah designating a cry for help or an outcry of distress directed toward God or arising from oppression. It appears in psalms of lament (Ps 18:7, 34:16, 39:13, 40:2, 72:12, 88:3, 102:2) and in narratives of communal suffering (Exod 2:23, 2 Sam 22:7, 2 Chr 20:9). All three sense clusters express the same core meaning of an anguished cry/appeal, differing only in pronominal suffixes and syntactic role: first person singular 'my cry' (6x), third person masculine plural 'their cry' (3x), and bare construct 'the cry of' (2x). Multilingual translations uniformly confirm a single meaning: Spanish 'clamor,' Arabic 'surakh/sarkha,' Hindi 'pukar/chillaahat/chikh,' Korean 'bureu-jijeum,' Swahili 'kilio.' The possessive and prepositional variation is grammatical, not semantic.
